systemPrompt:
You are an expert at planning interactive 3D visualizations for textbook figures.

PRIMARY CONTEXT:
The generated figure will be embedded alongside the original in a PDF reader. It should look recognizably like the source figure — same general geometry, viewpoint, labels, and proportions — but does not need to be a pixel-perfect inline replacement. Some additional controls or layout breathing room are fine if they genuinely help the learner.

INTERACTION PALETTE — choose the interactions that best fit the concept. Pick the fewest that genuinely serve the learning goal; more is not better. In "teaches", say what the learner understands, not what the control does.

• orbit / drag — rotate/move the scene. When depth or 3D shape IS the concept.
• hover — reveal a label on demand. When showing every label at once clutters.
• click — highlight one element. When focus on one part of a busy scene matters.
• slider — sweep one continuous variable. When dragging it visibly transforms the figure.
• toggle — switch between 2+ named views. For before/after or dual views (e.g. spatial ↔ frequency).
• button / state — step through discrete phases. When distinct stages should be visited deliberately.
• animation — self-playing motion. When the concept is inherently dynamic and a slider can't convey it.
• equation_input — learner types math, parsed at runtime. When "change the formula, reshape the output" (integrand, boundary, kernel); each field maps to one curve/quantity; catch parse errors inline.
• code_editor — learner writes/debugs an algorithm; the figure replays its execution frame by frame. Use ONLY when the concept IS a procedure whose intermediate states carry the lesson — heapify, one pass of a sort, a graph traversal, gradient descent, scanline fill — i.e. the question a learner has is "in what order does it touch the data, and why". Needs state small enough to draw whole (~30 elements) and an algorithm expressible in ~20 lines against a handful of operations. Do NOT use it for a continuous parameter (that is a slider), a formula the learner retypes (equation_input), or a static structure with no execution (hover/click). Choose it over animation when the learner should be able to get the procedure WRONG and watch where it diverges.

Output ONLY valid JSON (no markdown, no explanation):
{
  "projection_type": "perspective | axonometric | oblique",
  "camera_view": { "azimuthDeg": <perspective only — 0=side · 45=three-quarter · 90=front-on>, "elevationDeg": <perspective only — 0=eye-level · 20-35=slightly above · 90=top-down>, "rollDeg": 0, "heightFraction": <0.5 default · up to 0.75 to fill the frame> },
  "axis_screen_angles": <axonometric only — null for a flat 2D plot/diagram with no 3D depth (front-on view); omit this field entirely for a 3D axonometric figure (renderer uses a standard isometric pose)>,
  "elements": ["exhaustive list of every geometric element visible in the figure that must be recreated in 3D"],
  "interactions": [
    { "id": "uniqueCamelCaseId", "type": "orbit | drag | hover | click | slider | toggle | button | state | animation | equation_input | code_editor", "teaches": "what the learner understands", "...": "plus ONLY that type's fields — see INTERACTION FIELDS below" }
  ],
  "demo_steps": [
    {
      "title": "Step name shown in UI",
      "narration": "What the learner sees and understands at this step — one or two sentences",
      "state": { "interactionId": value }
    }
  ],
  "geometry_notes": "Approximate world-space scale (e.g. 'cube ~2 units side, axes span ±3'), dominant colors from the source, and any domain-specific formula or value needed for correctness.",
  "notes": "Three.js / rendering technique notes (distinct from geometry_notes)"
}

INTERACTION FIELDS — every interaction object has "id" (unique camelCase), "type", and "teaches". Add ONLY the fields listed for its type; never attach a "range" to anything but a slider.

"type" MUST be exactly one of these 11 strings: "orbit" · "drag" · "hover" · "click" · "slider" · "toggle" · "button" · "state" · "animation" · "equation_input" · "code_editor""

• orbit / drag / hover / click — no extra fields.
• animation      — "label", optional "loop": true | false.
• slider         — "label", "range": [min, max, step], "default": <number>.
• toggle         — "label", "options": ["A", "B", ...], "default": "A"   (a plain on/off toggle may drop "options" and use "default": true | false).
• button / state — "label", "states": ["idle", "running", "done"], "default": "idle".
• equation_input — "label", "fields": [ { "id": "...", "label": "f(x) =", "default": "sin(x)", "variables": ["x"], "domain": [min, max], "role": "integrand | boundary | kernel | ..." } ]. "domain" is the x-range the field is plotted over; always supply it so the generator does not have to guess.
• code_editor    — "label",
                   "entry_point": "the one function the learner must define, e.g. buildMaxHeap(heap)",
                   "api": [ { "op": "greater(i, j)", "does": "true when A[i] > A[j]" }, { "op": "swap(i, j)", "does": "exchange two elements — the ONLY way to mutate" }, ... ],
                   "frame": "what one recorded step shows, e.g. 'the whole array plus the 1-2 indices the op touched'",
                   "input": { "label": "Initial array", "default": "4, 1, 3, 2, 16, 9, 10" },
                   "sample_code": "<correct implementation, as a string>",
                   optional "buggy_code": "<plausible near-miss, with a comment naming the bug>",
                   "success_check": "the property the final state must satisfy, e.g. 'every parent >= both of its children'".
  Design the "api" first and keep it minimal: 4–7 ops covering read, compare, mutate, and annotate (a note/mark op for the learner's own commentary). Every state change must be reachable ONLY through an op — otherwise the replay has gaps. The learner writes algorithm logic, never drawing code.

demo_steps "state" may set values for slider, toggle, and button/state interactions only; code_editor and equation_input are seeded by their sample_code / fields defaults, not by demo_steps.

Rules:
- PROJECTION TYPE: pick whichever the source most resembles. Do not measure angles off the image — the renderer applies a fixed standard pose for each type, so a coarse visual call is enough. Spend your effort on ELEMENTS and INTERACTIONS instead; camera is a quick classification, not a measurement task.
  • "perspective" — depth edges clearly converge toward a vanishing point, or a single object's own far end reads smaller than its near end. Judge within one object; a row of separate same-shape objects that merely shrink (e.g. neural-net layers) is not perspective.
  • "oblique" — one face is drawn true (an undistorted rectangle: right angles, horizontal/vertical edges intact) while depth recedes off it along a single diagonal — e.g. stacked feature maps/filter banks drawn as offset same-size copies.
  • "axonometric" — the default for everything else: any other 3D-looking figure (axes tilted, no true face), or a flat 2D plot/diagram (set "axis_screen_angles": null for these).
- CAMERA VIEW: camera_view sets framing only. azimuthDeg/elevationDeg apply to perspective only: azimuthDeg 0 side, 45 three-quarter, 90 front-on; elevationDeg 0 eye-level, 10–20 low-angle, 25–35 moderate three-quarter, 90 top-down. rollDeg is usually 0. heightFraction is how much of the frame the figure should fill (0.5 default, up to 0.75).
- DEMO STEPS: include when the concept has 2+ distinct phases the learner should visit in sequence, each step driving one named configuration of the interaction state. Use [] for a single continuous exploration with no natural sequence.
- GEOMETRY NOTES: always fill this in — it is what stops the generator guessing sizes and getting the zoom wrong. Cover:
  • world-space dimensions, and for oblique/axonometric figures give each box explicitly as X × Y × Z world units, naming which source dimension each axis carries (+X is screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z the receding diagonal).
  • the colour palette, with hex codes where determinable from the source.
  • any formula or numeric range the generator needs to be mathematically correct.
  • POSITION AND ORIENTATION for each element as read off the source — which way it points, what angle it sits at, which side of another element it is on. Read this off the image; do not infer layout from general knowledge of the concept. A generic, plausible-looking arrangement is the failure mode the generator falls into whenever geometry_notes covers only dimensions.
  • for a repeated shape with a stated per-element value (channel count, layer size, category), an explicit number for each element's varying dimension tied to that value — equal values get equal size, even across sequence position — rather than a described trend.
- MULTI-PART FIGURES: if the source contains multiple labeled panels ((a)/(b)/(c), side-by-side comparisons, before/after pairs, sequential diagrams), do NOT recreate them all simultaneously in the initial view. Show one panel by default and link the rest through a single interaction — a toggle, tab, or slider — so the learner actively moves between parts. The transition itself should teach the comparison or progression.
- Prefer interactions that expose relationships in the figure rather than generic controls.

Figure: CNX_UPhysics_11_04_Precess

AUTHOR-PROVIDED INTERACTION REQUESTS:
Requested interactions:
- Animation for playing the top's precession: the learner starts the motion, the L arrow keeps its length while its tip sweeps the dashed circle and dL advances tangentially, making clear that torque changes the direction of angular momentum rather than its magnitude.
- Slider for the tilt angle theta: the learner increases or decreases the lean of the top, the L sin theta radius and the small d phi construction resize together, showing how the geometry of the tilted angular momentum sets the precession step.
- Slider for torque magnitude: the dL arrow length changes while L keeps its length, showing that torque redirects angular momentum during precession rather than simply making it longer.

Source file:
OpenStax University Physics, chapter 11: Angular Momentum

Use these requested interactions when forming the plan. Use the image to recover visual structure, layout, labels, camera/view cues, and missing visible elements.

Planner context:
This figure is a single three-dimensional diagram of a spinning top together with the vectors that govern its precession. A coordinate frame is drawn with z vertical, y to the right, and x angled toward the lower left, meeting at the origin O where the point of the top rests. The top is a rounded, banded body in blue and orange capped by a short cylindrical stem, its symmetry axis tilted away from z by the angle theta. A heavy black arrow labeled r runs from O to the center of mass, marked with an X and labeled 'CM', where a red arrow labeled 'M g' points straight down. From that same point an orange arrow labeled tau extends outward and slightly upward, with a curved leader to the expression 'tau = r x M g'. A green loop labeled omega circles the stem to give the spin sense, and a long orange arrow labeled L lies along the tilted axis, reaching a dashed horizontal circle drawn above the top. On that circle a radial orange arrow labeled 'L sin theta' and a tangential arrow labeled 'dL = tau dt' meet at a small angle marked 'd phi', while a curved black arrow labeled omega sub p at the upper left gives the direction of precession. Placing the torque perpendicular to L lets the reader see that the tip of L sweeps around the circle instead of tipping over. The construction sets up the calculation of how fast a gravitationally torqued top precesses about the vertical.

CONTEXT FROM TEXTBOOK:

A coordinate frame is drawn with z vertical, y to the right, and x angled toward the lower left, meeting at the origin O where the point of the top rests. The top is a rounded, banded body in blue and orange capped by a short cylindrical stem, its symmetry axis tilted away from z by the angle theta. A heavy black arrow labeled r runs from O to the center of mass, marked with an X and labeled 'CM', where a red arrow labeled 'M g' points straight down. From that same point an orange arrow labeled tau extends outward and slightly upward, with a curved leader to the expression 'tau = r x M g'. A green loop labeled omega circles the stem to give the spin sense, and a long orange arrow labeled L lies along the tilted axis, reaching a dashed horizontal circle drawn above the top. On that circle a radial orange arrow labeled 'L sin theta' and a tangential arrow labeled 'dL = tau dt' meet at a small angle marked 'd phi', while a curved black arrow labeled omega sub p at the upper left gives the direction of precession. Placing the torque perpendicular to L lets the reader see that the tip of L sweeps around the circle instead of tipping over. The construction sets up the calculation of how fast a gravitationally torqued top precesses about the vertical.

PROJECTION TYPE: axonometric
Use ordinary orthographic projection: setCameraView({ projection: 'orthographic', axisScreenAngles, heightFraction }). If the plan gives axis_screen_angles: null (a flat 2D plot/diagram), pass axisScreenAngles: null for a front-on view. Otherwise the plan does not measure per-figure angles — use a standard isometric pose: axisScreenAngles: { x: 30, z: 30 }. The source image is a PROJECTION of a 3D object: rebuild the true object — a rectangle stays a rectangle in world space — and let the camera do the projecting. Never bake the drawn parallelogram into the geometry, and never shear geometry. Omit zoom and call setCameraView after all geometry is added — the scaffold auto-fits from the projected bounding box.

ELEMENTS TO RECREATE IN 3D:
  - Coordinate axes: vertical z-axis (arrow up, label 'z'), horizontal y-axis to the right (label 'y'), x-axis receding toward the lower-left/viewer (label 'x'), meeting at origin labeled 'O'
  - Spinning top body: rounded teardrop/bell of revolution with pointed tip at O, widest near its upper third, tilted from the z-axis by angle theta
  - Alternating horizontal bands on the top body (light blue and orange stripes following the surface of revolution)
  - Short cylindrical stem on the top's upper face, coaxial with the top's symmetry axis
  - Green curved arrow loop around the stem labeled 'ω' giving the spin sense
  - Black thick arrow from O to the center of mass labeled 'r⃗'
  - Black X marker at the center of mass with label 'CM'
  - Red downward arrow from CM labeled 'M g⃗' (weight)
  - Orange arrow from CM pointing outward and slightly upward, perpendicular to r⃗ and to g⃗, labeled 'τ⃗'
  - Curved black leader line from the τ arrow to the expression 'τ⃗ = r⃗ × M g⃗'
  - Long orange arrow along the tilted symmetry axis from the top up to the dashed circle, labeled 'L⃗'
  - Dashed horizontal circle traced by the tip of L⃗, drawn above the top and centered on the z-axis
  - Orange radial arrow in the plane of the dashed circle from the z-axis to the tip of L⃗, labeled 'L sin θ'
  - Orange tangential arrow at the tip of L⃗, labeled 'dL⃗ = τ⃗ dt'
  - Small angle arc between the radial arrow and the advanced radius, labeled 'dφ'
  - Faint second radius of the dashed circle showing the advanced position after dφ
  - Curved black arrow at the upper left around the z-axis labeled 'ω_p' giving the precession sense
  - Angle arc at the origin between the z-axis and r⃗, labeled 'θ'

GEOMETRY NOTES (world-space scale, color palette, and any formula/value needed for correctness — build to these so sizes, zoom, and colors match the source; do not guess dimensions the notes already specify):
World units: origin O at (0,0,0) with +Z up (drawn as the 'z' axis), +X to screen-right (the figure's 'y' axis, arrow length 3.5), and the figure's 'x' axis along the receding diagonal toward the viewer's lower-left (length 2.5). z-axis arrow extends to +6.0. Top body: surface of revolution about a tilted symmetry axis through O, total length ~3.6 from the point at O to its flat upper face, maximum radius ~1.35 occurring at ~0.65 of its length; profile is a sharp point at O flaring into a rounded bell then tapering slightly to the flat top (teardrop inverted). Symmetry axis tilted by θ (default 25°, range 10–60°) from +Z, leaning toward +X (screen-right) with the precession phase rotating that lean direction about Z. Stem cylinder: radius 0.18, length 0.85, coaxial, sitting on the top face. CM lies on the symmetry axis at distance r = 1.9 from O (marked with a black X). L arrow: orange, drawn along the symmetry axis from about z=2.3 on that axis out to the dashed circle, total drawn length ~3.0, tip at height z = L cos θ with L = 4.8 world units; the dashed circle therefore sits at z ≈ 4.35 (for θ=25°) with radius L sin θ ≈ 2.0 centered on the z-axis. Radial arrow 'L sin θ' drawn in that horizontal plane from the axis to the L tip; tangential arrow 'dL = τ dt' at the tip, perpendicular to the radius, length 0.5·(torque slider) — never changes |L|; dφ = |dL|/(L sin θ) shown as a small arc between the current radius and a faint advanced radius. Curved ω_p arrow: black, ~120° arc of radius 2.4 around the z-axis at z≈5.4, upper-left, counter-clockwise seen from above. Green ω loop: ~300° arc of radius 0.35 around the stem. Mg arrow: red, from CM straight down (−Z) length 1.0. τ arrow: orange, from CM along the direction r̂ × (−ẑ) (horizontal, perpendicular to the lean plane), length 1.1·(torque slider), drawn slightly foreshortened upward-right in the default view; curved black leader from its tip down-right to the label 'τ⃗ = r⃗ × M g⃗'. θ arc of radius 0.8 at O between +Z and r. Colors: top body blue #7FB3C9 with lighter highlight #A9CEDD, orange bands #F2C075, orange vectors/labels #EF8420, red weight #C0392B, green spin loop #7FA82F, black axes, r arrow, dashed circle and ω_p. Precession: tip of L advances at ω_p = M g r sinθ /(L sinθ) = M g r / L; drive the animation with ω_p ∝ torqueSlider / L, independent of θ.

DISCRETE CONTROLS (implement every one of these in #ui, each must work independently):
[
  {
    "id": "orbit",
    "type": "orbit",
    "teaches": "That τ, r and Mg are mutually perpendicular in three dimensions and that the tip of L really moves on a horizontal circle, not in the plane of the page"
  },
  {
    "id": "precess",
    "type": "animation",
    "teaches": "That the torque, always perpendicular to L, changes only the direction of the angular momentum: |L| stays fixed while its tip sweeps the dashed circle and the whole top (with r, Mg and τ) rotates about z",
    "label": "Play precession",
    "loop": true
  },
  {
    "id": "theta",
    "type": "slider",
    "teaches": "That the lean angle sets the geometry of precession: the circle radius L sin θ, the moment arm of gravity, and therefore the size of the dφ step all change together with θ",
    "label": "Tilt angle θ (deg)",
    "range": [
      10,
      60,
      1
    ],
    "default": 25
  },
  {
    "id": "torque",
    "type": "slider",
    "teaches": "That a larger torque lengthens dL = τ dt and so advances L through a bigger dφ per step, while |L| itself is unchanged — torque redirects angular momentum instead of growing it",
    "label": "Torque magnitude τ (relative)",
    "range": [
      0.2,
      2,
      0.05
    ],
    "default": 1
  }
]

DEMO STEPS (tween through these using goToStep(); each step drives the controls above):
[
  {
    "title": "Static construction",
    "narration": "The top leans by θ from the vertical. r runs from the pivot O to the CM, gravity Mg pulls straight down there, and τ = r × Mg points horizontally, perpendicular to both.",
    "state": {
      "theta": 25,
      "torque": 1,
      "precess": false
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "The dL step",
    "narration": "Because τ is perpendicular to L, the increment dL = τ dt is tangent to the dashed circle of radius L sin θ. The tip of L turns through dφ = dL /(L sin θ) without L getting longer.",
    "state": {
      "theta": 25,
      "torque": 1.6,
      "precess": false
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Increase the lean",
    "narration": "Raising θ widens the circle L sin θ and increases gravity's moment arm; watch how both the radius and the angular step dφ respond.",
    "state": {
      "theta": 50,
      "torque": 1,
      "precess": false
    }
  },
  {
    "title": "Let it precess",
    "narration": "Run the motion: L keeps a constant length and constant tilt while its tip sweeps the circle at the precession rate ω_p = Mgr /(L) — the whole top rotates about the vertical.",
    "state": {
      "theta": 30,
      "torque": 1,
      "precess": true
    }
  }
]

CAMERA VIEW (framing only). Call setCameraView({ projection, ...these }) AFTER all geometry is added. Keep the projection MECHANISM from PROJECTION TYPE above (orthographic / sheared-oblique / perspective). For perspective these params set the pose (azimuth/elevation/roll); for the two parallel projections pose is a standard default (see PROJECTION TYPE above), and these params set only roll and framing (heightFraction):
{
  "heightFraction": 0.72
}

NOTES: Build the top as a LatheGeometry from a hand-specified profile, grouped with the stem and rotated by θ about the receding-horizontal axis then spun by the precession phase about Z; parent everything (body, r, CM, Mg, τ, L) to one precession Group so a single phase rotation moves the whole assembly consistently. Use ArrowHelper or custom cone+cylinder meshes for the vectors so head size stays constant as lengths change. Dashed circle: LineDashedLine with computeLineDistances, regenerated when θ changes. Labels as sprite/CSS2D overlays with MathJax-style italic glyphs ('z','y','x','O','CM','θ','ω','ω_p','L','L sin θ','dφ','dL = τ dt','r','M g','τ = r × M g'). Curved leader for the τ label as a QuadraticBezierCurve3 tube or fat line. Render the top with MeshStandardMaterial, slight flatShading off, plus a subtle ambient + key light from upper-left to match the shaded source artwork; enable a light background and no ground plane. Keep |L| constant in code (only its direction changes) so the torque slider visibly alters dL and dφ but not the arrow length.

Follow the interaction plan above.
